docs.description: a child component element is handed a prop that is a new reference on every render
docs.why: A prop allocated in the parent's render body — an object literal, an array literal, an inline arrow — is a different reference on every render of the parent. That costs nothing on a host element, but on a child *component* it defeats every identity check downstream: a `React.memo` comparison can never bail out, and the value poisons any dependency array the child lists it in. reactant cannot see through the `React.memo` wrapper (#64), so this rule reports the unstable reference and leaves the memo question to review — the fact it certifies is the freshness, not the waste.
docs.fix: Hoist the value out of the render body, wrap it in `useMemo`/`useCallback`, or pass the primitive parts instead of a wrapper object. Note that `children` is a fresh element tree on every render by construction and is reported here too — the `jsx_props` relation carries no guard on the prop's name, so the rule cannot skip it. Keep this at `info` until that guard exists.

rules.message: {anchor.name} is given {anchor.prop} as a {anchor.identity} value — every identity check on that prop downstream (a memo comparison, a deps array) is guaranteed to miss

docs.description: an effect that registers something outliving it lists a dependency that is a new reference every render
docs.why: The dependency never compares equal, so the effect tears down and re-runs on every render of the component. When the body only writes `document.title` that is waste; when it opens a socket, starts an interval or fires a request, it is a resource leak or a traffic multiplier — one registration per render, forever. The unstable dependency is often a prop the parent allocates inline, so the fix belongs in the caller, not here.
docs.fix: Depend on the primitive fields the effect actually reads (`[query.topic, query.limit]`), or make the caller stabilise the value with `useMemo` before passing it.
docs.example: useEffect(() => { fetchFeed(query).then(setItems) }, [query])  // query allocated by the parent

rules.message: this effect registers something that outlives it, and its dependency {dep.path} is {dep.stability} — the registration is torn down and redone on every render

docs.description: a function argument of useSyncExternalStore returns a freshly allocated reference
docs.why: React calls `getSnapshot` after every render and compares the result with `Object.is`. A snapshot function that returns `[]`, `{}`, or the result of `.map`/`.filter`/`.slice`/a spread hands back a new reference every call, so the store always looks changed: React re-renders, calls the snapshot again, and loops. React's own development warning for this is "The result of getSnapshot should be cached to avoid an infinite loop"; in production it is a pinned core.
docs.fix: Return a reference the store caches until it actually mutates, hoist the empty case to a module constant (`const EMPTY = []`), and do the derivation in a `useMemo` keyed on the snapshot instead of inside it.

rules.message: {anchor.name} is passed a function that returns {arg.returns} — `Object.is` sees a changed snapshot after every render, which is the documented infinite-loop shape
